findings.title: Security Advisory: Update BTCPay Server to 2.4.2 Immediately
findings.summary_md: BTCPay Server disclosed a critical vulnerability present in all versions prior to 2.4.2, including 2.4.2 release candidates, that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker obtain LND `.macaroon` credential files and take control of an LND node to move funds. The project confirmed attackers exploited it, users were affected and funds were stolen, and credited Craig Raw with responsible disclosure. BTCPay Server's on-chain wallets, including hot wallets, were not affected by this issue; users were urged to update to 2.4.2 and LND 0.21.1.

findings.title: Release 2.4.7
findings.summary_md: Nicolas Dorier released BTCPay Server 2.4.7 on October 29, 2026 as an emergency security update. It fixes 85 security findings from Anthropic's Frontier OSS scanner, rated 1 critical, 13 high, 52 medium and 19 low, spanning merchant isolation, payouts, authentication and payment accounting. The release notes say updating is highly recommended, especially for servers shared by multiple merchants.

findings.title: Bitcoin Payment Processor Btcpay Hit by Hot Wallet Theft Reports
findings.summary_md: BTCPay Server issued an emergency shutdown warning on November 1, 2026 after reports that attackers were draining bitcoin from hot wallets on self-hosted payment servers. Founder Nicolas Dorier linked the reported compromises to versions predating 2.4.2 and said public servers running 2.4.7 had not been attacked. At press time no total loss estimate or complete technical account had been published.

findings.title: BTCPay Server Hack Drains Hot Wallets Days After Binance
findings.summary_md: Attackers had been draining hot wallets on self-hosted BTCPay Server installations since October 30, 2026, and on November 1 the project told operators to switch servers off while it searched for the entry point. The project later traced the drains to version 2.4.1 or older, and Bitquery estimated about 1.63 million USD in bitcoin and litecoin left merchant wallets, with each merchant bearing its own loss.
